newsitem.title: POLAND: EX-PM ATTACKS POLISH PRESIDENT OVER CONSTITUTION.
newsitem.headline: EX-PM ATTACKS POLISH PRESIDENT OVER CONSTITUTION.

text.p: Former prime minister Jan Olszewski on Sunday attacked Poland's ex-communist President Aleksander Kwasniewski for allegedly deceiving the nation ahead of this month's constitutiuonal referendum.

Olszewski, the leader of the rightist Reconstruction of Poland movement (ROP), said the new draft constitution being sent to citizens together with a letter by Kwasniewski were "manipulative propaganda designed to mislead citizens," PAP news agency reported.
It will become law only if approved in a popular referendum on May 25, but in his letter Kwasniewski called it "the Constitution of the Republic of Poland," he told a news conference.
He is misleading the public by failing to state that it is still only a draft, Olszewski argued.
ROP has been campaigning to let voters choose between the draft adopted by Poland's leftist-doiminated parliament and an independent version drawn up by the right-leaning Solidarity movement.
As things now stand, Poles will only be able to approve or reject the draft constitution being promoted by Kwasniewski.
Earlier on Sunday, Kwasniewski had expressed dismay at the allegation by Poland's Catholic bishops that the consitution raised "serious moral objections."
He made the remarks on public radio's political-affairs breakfast show, saying he had hoped the Church would remain neutral towards the consitution.
Political emotions are hotting up in Poland ahead of the referendum and parliamentary elections expected in September.
On the breakfast show, Kwasniewski said the elections would probably take place on September 14.
